scenes.headline: How a reasoning loop is measured, and what Nex-N2.6 fixed
scenes.sub: Repetition, tool names and benchmarks, read against the base model
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Dorrit! Nex-N2.6 is an open agent model that says it loops far less, and never calls a tool that isn't there. Let's see what those claims measure.

scenes.title: When reasoning loops
scenes.sub: A chain of thought that folds back on itself

scenes.title: Where a loop hides in an agent

steps.say: An agent gets a request, with the list of tools it may use, and starts to reason.

steps.term: Harness: the loop that runs tool calls
steps.say: It calls a tool. The harness runs it and hands back the output, and the model reasons again.
A loop is when the reasoning folds back on itself. The same check, written again and again. The tool call never comes, and the episode times out.

scenes.title: Scoring one trace, the article's toy way

steps.say: Take the looping trace from the article. Split it into words. Seventy-nine of them.

steps.term: N-gram: a run of n tokens
steps.say: Slide a window of six words along it.
Any window that already appeared earlier is a repeat. Mark every word inside one. Thirty-nine words get marked.
So the repeated share is forty-nine point four percent.
Set the threshold at thirty percent, and this trace is flagged as a loop.

scenes.title: From traces to a rate

parts.note: traces whose repeated share passes tau
parts.say: Do that for every trace in a test set, and count how many get flagged.
Divide by the number of traces. That is a repetition rate.

scenes.say: Every choice moves this number: the window length, the threshold, and whether a repeated tool error counts. Nex has not published its choices.

scenes.title: Why models loop
scenes.say: Why do models loop at all? The research names four pushes.

items.say: Decoding for the likeliest text walks straight into cycles.
Each copy of a sentence makes the next copy more likely.
Reinforcement learning drains the policy's entropy, so it has fewer ways out.
And if long traces earn reward, looping is the cheapest way to be long.

scenes.title: Where the drop came from
scenes.sub: Two changes at once: a new base, and Nex's training
scenes.say: Chapter two. Where the drop came from.

scenes.title: Reasoning repetition rate, lower is better
scenes.say: The launch post says repetition fell from sixteen percent to one point six. But N2.6 is built on a different base. The base alone was already at six percent.

scenes.credit: chart from Nex's post on X

steps.say: Nex's own chart prints that base column.

steps.note: 6.0 is the base, on Nex's own suite
steps.say: Most of the fall from sixteen to six is already there when Nex runs its suite on the base model. Nex's own training takes it from six to one point six. That step is real.

scenes.title: Selection is not success
scenes.sub: What a valid tool name does and does not tell you
scenes.say: Chapter three. Selection is not success.

scenes.title: The gates one tool call passes

steps.say: Every request lists the tools the harness provides. The model has to use only those.

steps.term: Valid selection: the name is on the list
steps.say: Nex's metric checks one gate: is the tool name on the list? Across nine hundred and fifty-six contexts, N2.6 passed every time.
It does not check the gates after it. Was it the right tool for this step? Were the arguments right?
And a task is many calls in a row. A model that always called the shell would still score a hundred percent.

left.title: Nex's table
left.say: Nex's table puts DeepSeek V four point one Flash at eighty-two point seven, behind N2.6.

right.title: DeepSeek's own card
right.say: DeepSeek's own card says ninety point six, and eighty-two point seven sits under its older model.

scenes.credit: Google DeepMind's MKA dataset, RF task input
scenes.title: What a harder benchmark grades

steps.say: Compare a harder benchmark. Google DeepMind's Multimodal Knowledge Agent hands the agent real files, like these spectrum plots from a chip design.
The agent must classify each marked spur and decide whether the chip can tape out. Its rubric grades the answer, not the tool name.

scenes.text: A repetition rate is only as good as its window and threshold, and a valid tool name is a gate, not success.
scenes.say: A repetition rate is only as good as its window and its threshold. And a valid tool name is a gate, not success. Read both against the base model.

recap: A loop is repeated n-grams past a threshold
The base was at 6.0; Nex took it to 1.6
A valid tool name is a gate, not success
scenes.say: To recap. A loop is repeated windows past a threshold. The base was already at six percent, and Nex took it to one point six. And a valid tool name is a gate, not success.
